item.title: Mise
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Mise
https://mise.jdx.dev/
Your dev env,already prepped. One tool to manage languages, env vars, and tasks per project, reproducibly.

Everything in its place, before you code.
In a professional kitchen, mise en place is the ritual of prep: knives sharpened, onions diced, stock warm, station clean. The work before the work.
mise does the same for your dev env. It activates the right language versions, loads the right env vars, and wires up the right tasks for the commands you run.

item.title: dobi
item.author: emecas
item.description:
dobi Documentation
A build automation tool for Docker applications.
https://dnephin.github.io/dobi/

A build automation tool for Docker applications.
Keep your project tasks organized, portable, repeatable, and fast with dobi. Define the resources and tasks required to build, test, and release your project in a dobi.yaml and run them with dobi TASK.

Use Cases

examples/minimal-docker-image - building a minimal docker image, that does not contain build/compile dependencies. This is sometimes referred to as “squashing” an image.
examples/tag-images - tag images with metadata (git sha, git branch, datetime, and version)
examples/project-setup - prompt users for configuration and generate a .env file if it doesn’t exist.
examples/init-db-with-rails - load database tables and fixtures from rails models and create a database image and development environment.
examples/init-named-volume - create or update the files in a named docker volume.
examples/inline-dockerfile - inline Dockerfiles in the dobi.yaml to reduce the number of build files.
examples/env-vars - populate environment variables from job task output

item.title: xc
item.author: emecas
item.description:
xc - Simple, Convenient, Docs-based task runner.
https://xcfile.dev/

xc is a task runner similar to Make or npm run, that aims to be more discoverable and approachable.

The problem xc is intended to solve is scripts maintained separately from their documentation. Often a Makefile or a package.json will contain some useful scripts for developing on a project, then the README.md will surface and describe these scripts. In such a case, since the documentation is separate, it may not be updated when scripts are changed or added. xc aims to solve this by defining the scripts inline with the documentation.

item.title: OpenTelemetri
item.author: emecas
item.description:
OpenTelemetry
https://opentelemetry.io/
The open standard for telemetry

OpenTelemetry (OTel) is a leading open-source framework designed to help developers monitor and understand the performance of complex, cloud-native applications. It was created by merging two major projects, **OpenTracing** and **OpenCensus**, under the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF).

Here is a breakdown of why it’s a big deal in the software world:

### Core Benefits

* **Vendor Neutrality:** You can instrument your code once and send your data to any backend (like Prometheus, Jaeger, or commercial tools). This prevents “vendor lock-in,” allowing you to switch providers without rewriting your application code.
* **Unified Signals:** It brings together **Traces** (the journey of a request), **Metrics** (performance data over time), and **Logs** (timestamped events) into a single, correlated view.
* **Broad Support:** It offers native SDKs for over 12 programming languages and features more than 900 integrations.

item.title: Apache Superset
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Apache Superset
https://superset.apache.org/
Apache Superset is an open-source modern data exploration and visualization platform.

Key features

• 40+ pre-installed visualizations
• Support for drag-and-drop and SQL queries
• Data caching for the faster load time of charts and dashboards
• Jinja templating and dashboard filters for creating interactive dashboards
• CSS templates to customize charts and dashboards to your brand’s look and feel
• Semantic layer for SQL data transformations
• Cross-filters, drill-to-detail, and drill-by features for deeper data analysis
• Virtual datasets for ad-hoc data exploration
• Access to new functionalities through feature flags

item.title: Apache Shenyu
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Apache Shenyu
Java native API Gateway for service proxy, protocol conversion and API governance.
https://shenyu.apache.org/

https://github.com/apache/shenyu

Feature List

- Language: provides .NET, Python, Go, Java client for API register
- Proxy: Support for Apache® Dubbo™, Spring Cloud, gRPC, Motan, SOFA, TARS, WebSocket, MQTT
- Security: Sign, OAuth 2.0, JSON Web Tokens, WAF plugin
- API governance: Request, response, parameter mapping, Hystrix, RateLimiter plugin
- Observability: Tracing, metrics, logging plugin
- Extensions: Plugin hot-swapping, dynamic loading
- Dashboard: Dynamic traffic control, visual backend for user menu permissions
- Cluster: NGINX, Docker, Kubernetes

item.title: Hey
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Hey
https://github.com/rakyll/hey

hey is a tiny program that sends some load to a web application.

hey was originally called boom and was influenced from Tarek Ziade’s tool at tarekziade/boom.

Using the same name was a mistake as it resulted in cases where binary name conflicts created confusion.
To preserve the name for its original owner, we renamed this project to hey.

Previously known as github.com/rakyll/boom.

Source: commit a637379 in My-Notes.

item.title: Krita
item.author: emecas
item.description:
Krita
https://krita.org/
Krita is a free and open source painting program for new and experienced artists. It offers multiple brush types, layers, animation tools, online resources, a supportive community and more.

Features:

- Clean and Flexible Interface

An intuitive user interface that stays out of your way. The dockers and panels can be moved and customized for your specific workflow. Once you have your setup, you can save it as your own workspace. You can also create your own shortcuts for commonly used tools.
